note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Progressive numbness and tingling in left arm/hand; patient associates onset with starting a boxing class three weeks ago.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Initial mild tingling → worsening over ≈ 2 weeks to constant numbness from elbow to hand.  
  • One prior transient (≈ 20 min) episode of partial visual loss in left eye a few weeks ago.  
  • Symptoms not relieved by massage, warm baths, or ibuprofen.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: none reported.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: none.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: none.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: left-eye transient visual field loss only.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: none.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: none.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: none.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: denies significant neck pain.  
  • Jaw discomfort was entered on symptom checker but not stressed during visit.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Recent “bad cold/flu” lasting ~2 weeks preceding neurologic symptoms.  
  • Massage, warm baths, ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) provided no relief.
  • No prior ED visits, injections, or hospitalizations for similar complaints.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies: not documented.  
  • Medications: Ibuprofen PRN (dose/frequency not documented), vitamin D (dose not documented), intermittent iron supplement, melatonin PRN. No rescue medications or auto-injector.
- Any relevant social context:
  • 46-year-old right-handed female; exercises regularly; recently began boxing; occasional binge alcohol use. Consult conducted privately from secure location.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none reported.
- Airway/breathing: normal per history; no stridor or respiratory distress noted.
- Mental status: alert and interactive via video.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (tele-consultation; no physical or neurologic exam documented).
- Presence of another person: Patient alone during consultation.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Unilateral left-arm sensory deficit with subjective weakness and prior transient visual disturbance—concern for central neurologic pathology; less likely peripheral entrapment alone.
  Evidence summary: Progressive arm numbness (digits 2–4, palmar side) and weakness for 2 weeks; transient monocular visual loss; recent viral illness; no improvement with conservative measures.
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with DDx):
  1. Multiple sclerosis – optic-type visual event + evolving focal sensory deficit; age/sex fit; family autoimmune background. Opposing evidence: visual loss brief (20 min) and single limb involvement only.
  2. Cervical radiculopathy (probable C7) – dermatomal pattern after repetitive neck/upper-body strain; shoulder discomfort. Opposing evidence: no neck pain reported.
  3. Median nerve entrapment – classic palmar 2nd–4th digit paresthesia; repetitive wrist impact from boxing. Opposing evidence: proximal elbow/arm symptoms and overall limb weakness.
  (No ENT/allergic etiology suggested.)
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Urgent neurology referral initiated for MRI brain/spine and formal neurologic evaluation.
- Patient instructions:
  • Seek emergency care (call 911) if new or worsening weakness (especially legs), vision changes persisting > 30 min, severe headache, vomiting, seizures, or any loss of consciousness.
  • Continue routine activities cautiously; avoid further boxing or heavy upper-body exercise until evaluated.
- Follow-up:
  • Await neurology appointment; primary care to track referral status.  
  • Consider ENT review only if future airway, voice, or oropharyngeal symptoms emerge (none currently).
  • No medication changes at this stage; treatment decisions deferred to neurology after imaging.
- Education:
  • Discussed possible etiologies, prognosis, and importance of early evaluation.  
  • Reassured availability of disease-modifying therapies if MS confirmed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: complete allergy list; vital signs; focused neurologic examination; documentation of medication dosages/frequencies; cervical spine examination; ENT airway exam (not applicable in tele-visit).  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; occasional overlapping speech but clinically adequate.
